---
title: 'Tuturuuu Bot'
description: 'Local agent PR authorship, owner provisioning and credential boundaries.'
---

`tuturuuu-bot` is a private GitHub App owned by `tutur3u`, installed only on
`tutur3u/platform`. Its sole purpose is local agent feature-branch pushes and PR
creation. Release automation retains its own identity and credentials. The App's
webhook is inactive and it subscribes to no events.

## Owner provisioning checklist

Only the owner performs credential setup, outside agent sessions and recordings.

1. Review `.github/tuturuuu-bot/manifest.json`. Submit that JSON as the `manifest`
   form field in a **POST** to
   `https://github.com/organizations/tutur3u/settings/apps/new`, following the
   [GitHub manifest flow](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/sharing-github-apps/registering-a-github-app-from-a-manifest).
   A GET link does not submit the manifest. Use an owner-controlled form/callback,
   random `state`, and a local copy with its `redirect_url`; verify callback state.
   Exchange the temporary code at
   `POST https://api.github.com/app-manifests/{code}/conversions` within one hour.
   Route the credential-bearing response directly to the owner's credential
   manager, never terminal output, git, chat or an agent. No callback service is
   deployed here. If no trusted callback exists, use **Organization settings →
   Developer settings → GitHub Apps → New GitHub App**, transcribe the manifest,
   disable the webhook, select **Only on this account** and generate the key there.
2. Confirm the available slug is `tuturuuu-bot`, private visibility and exactly
   the permissions below. Click **Install App → tutur3u → Only select repositories
   → platform → Install**. Do not select all repositories. Record the numeric App
   ID and installation ID privately as configuration; these IDs are not secrets.
3. Import the private key through the owner-controlled Keychain Access interface
   into a generic password item with service `tuturuuu-bot-private-key`. Do not
   grant blanket application access. If using `security add-generic-password`,
   create it **without `-A` or `-T`**; never put the PEM on the command line or in
   shell history. Remove any automatically trusted applications in Access Control
   and require confirmation for access. Never click **Always Allow**. Approve
   **Allow** only for an expected operation after verifying its requester.
4. Set non-secret `TUTURUUU_BOT_APP_ID` and `TUTURUUU_BOT_INSTALLATION_ID` in the
   trusted local launcher session. No workflow in this change mints an App token.
   **Do not create `TUTURUUU_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` as an Actions repository secret or
   environment secret.** The key is needed only locally. A repo variable of the
   same App ID name is unnecessary for this local-only design.
5. Before any future workflow minting is considered, a dedicated GitHub
   environment is a **required precondition**: configure its deployment-branch
   policy for **main and production only**, protect it with owner review, put
   `TUTURUUU_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY` only in that environment, and require every minting
   job to declare `environment:`. Never put the key in a repository secret or
   allow arbitrary branch/fork code to consume it. This is future scope requiring
   owner approval; creating the environment or changing settings is not done here.
6. Recommended defense in depth: **platform → Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New
   tag ruleset**, target the actual release tag patterns (for example `v*` and
   package-prefixed release tags from Release Please), enable **Restrict updates**
   and **Restrict deletions**, and keep the App outside bypass lists. Confirm the
   selected patterns cover real tags and do not block first-time release tag
   creation. Only the owner applies repo settings; this PR does not apply them.
7. Add an owner-managed branch ruleset restricting updates to
   `release-please--branches--*`, with access limited to the intended release
   writer and no agent-bot bypass. Review creation/deletion protections as well.
   If the release PAT and agents share `vhpx`, GitHub cannot distinguish their
   processes through an actor-based ruleset; isolating the release writer's
   credentials/principal remains necessary. This PR does not apply the ruleset.
8. Verify a narrowly scoped push to an owned task branch, then PR creation. Check
   the PR author is `tuturuuu-bot[bot]`, its human approval gate remains required,
   and the token is revoked. Do not dispatch release/publication jobs to test this
   local identity. Do not retire `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN`: releases still use it.

## Permissions and retained identities

| App permission | Justification |
| --- | --- |
| Contents: write | Local agents push an explicitly named owned task branch. |
| Pull requests: write | Local agents create PRs. GitHub also permits review APIs at this level; the helper and policy prohibit approval. |
| Metadata: read | Required repository/installation metadata baseline. |

No issues permission is needed to create PRs. No actions, workflows, checks,
administration, deployments or secrets permission is granted. The bot is never a
ruleset bypass actor. The helper cannot push workflow files with this token;
workflow-changing work needs a separately authorized identity and review.

| Surface | Decision | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local task-branch pushes and agent PR creation | Use the App via the helper | Explicit contents/pull_requests subset; platform only |
| `release-please.yaml` | Retain `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` with existing `github.token` fallback | Existing release PAT includes workflow scope; never substitute the agent App |
| Package release dispatchers and TestFlight review queue | Retain `github.token` | Existing Actions job permissions; no App key or token minting |
| Release approval | Preserve main's original author allowlist and job approval token | Only `github-actions[bot]` is eligible; `vhpx` and arbitrary Bot authors remain ineligible |
| All other workflows and scripts | Retain existing identity | Job-bound tokens, service credentials or owning lane policy |

The release approval guard preserves the original `github-actions[bot]` author
allowlist, together with release-branch, commit-subject and generated-file gates.
A `type: Bot` flag does not confer authority. `vhpx`-authored release PRs remain
ineligible for automatic approval even if an override includes that login.
The workflow and core pin `RELEASE_PLEASE_AUTHORS` to `github-actions[bot]` only.

GitHub resolves `commit.author.login` from author email, which can be spoofed.
Matching that login and a generated-looking subject/file set is a heuristic, not
proof that release automation created or pushed the commit. The owner-managed
release-branch ruleset and isolated writer credentials are needed to restrict
who can update the branch. Neither the allowlist nor this PR establishes trusted
commit provenance. Existing self-review refusal remains a blocked outcome.

## Local usage

Run from trusted code on an owner-controlled macOS host:

```sh
node scripts/tuturuuu-bot-token.js --permissions contents=write -- git push origin HEAD:chore/my-task
node scripts/tuturuuu-bot-token.js --permissions contents=read,pull_requests=write -- gh pr create --head chore/my-task --repo tutur3u/platform
```

Git accepts exactly `git push origin HEAD:<task-branch>`. Task branches use the
repository's feature/fix/chore/docs and related authored prefixes; names use
letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and slash-separated components. The helper
rejects omitted/multiple refspecs, implicit destinations, protected/release/tag
refs, deletion refspecs, force options, `--delete`, `-d`, `--mirror`, `--all`,
`--tags`, `--receive-pack`, `--exec` and all other push flags. Git's normal
non-fast-forward checks remain in force. The wrapper replaces the `origin` label
with `https://github.com/tutur3u/platform.git` and sends exactly
`HEAD:refs/heads/<task-branch>`. It disables automatic tag following with
`push.followTags=false` and disables local hooks with both `--no-verify` and
`core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, so pre-push hooks do not receive the child token.

PR creation requires exactly one `--head <task-branch>` using the same task-branch
validation as pushes. Supported options are parsed before credential access;
missing/duplicate/ambiguous heads and another repository are refused. The helper
sets `GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1` to prevent interactive branch-push prompts. It accepts
only that `gh pr create` form and the constrained `git push` form. All
`gh pr review` invocations (including `--approve` and `-a`), token-inspection
commands, `gh api` and other executables are refused before Keychain access.
Only explicit `contents` and `pull_requests` scope inputs are accepted; metadata
read is implicit. It always requests repository `platform` and uses the fixed
GitHub API origin without redirects or automatic retries.

Private keys are read only with macOS `security find-generic-password`, signed
in memory and never supplied to the child. File/env private keys and token-printing
modes are forbidden. Installation tokens go only to the child environment.
Temporary Git credential config overrides cached personal credentials without
writing credentials/config to disk. The helper does not call `gh auth login` or
`gh auth setup-git`. Auth tracing/config override environment variables are stripped.
`GH_HOST` and the default `GH_REPO` are fixed; pass `--repo tutur3u/platform` to gh.
No 1Password adapter is implemented.

## Threat model, rotation and revocation

The trusted boundary includes the host user, Keychain ACLs, wrapper source, Node,
Git, gh, PATH, repository hooks/config, editor and child command. Keychain is not
an agent sandbox. Same-user processes may prompt for the same key, and a mistaken
Allow can release it. Never use Always Allow. A compromised same-user tool,
child, debugger or hook can steal memory/environment credentials. Recommended
future hardening is a **separate-user or biometric signing broker** that retains
the private key, requires user presence and enforces repository/permission/request
policy while returning only short-lived scoped tokens. That broker is not
implemented here; the current wrapper handles the key in its own process memory.

Child output is inherited, so a compromised child can print credentials. Local
push hooks are disabled; this does not sandbox the host tools or Git configuration. Never
use HTTP/shell tracing, credential inspection or commands that persist auth. Error
messages from signing, Keychain, API response bodies and subprocess exceptions are
replaced with fixed messages. The wrapper itself never logs or writes the key or
token. It preserves child status and attempts revocation on normal exit, child
failure and errors after minting. Requests have 15-second deadlines and the child
has a 50-minute deadline. Abrupt termination, host/network failure or an unknown
mint response may leave a token alive until expiry (within one hour). Do not
blindly replay an unknown push/PR outcome: inspect the remote state first.

For rotation, the owner creates a second key in App settings, privately replaces
the Keychain item, verifies a scoped operation, then deletes the old App key and
any temporary download. Removing a private key alone may not revoke issued
tokens. Explicitly revoke them or suspend the installation if needed. For an
emergency, **Organization settings → GitHub Apps → tuturuuu-bot → Suspend/Uninstall**,
delete compromised App keys/Keychain items, review the audit log and reconcile
writes before resuming. No Actions secret should exist to rotate in this design;
remove any leftover App repository secret from an earlier owner experiment.
Owner revocation/setting actions are never performed automatically by agents.

## Human review and follow-up

Bot-authored PRs are normal PRs. `vhpx` is a separate principal, so vhpx's approval
counts independently subject to repository rules. PR authorship comes from the
token used at creation; commit coauthor trailers do not determine it. This bootstrap
PR may use the existing identity until the App is provisioned.

The bot must never approve PRs or be a bypass actor. CODEOWNERS work in #6491
assigns sensitive paths to human `@vhpx`; it does not remove the App's underlying
GitHub review capability. After #6456 merges, its classifier lane should add a
**default-branch-code check that fails any PR approved by `tuturuuu-bot[bot]`**.
This is a required follow-up, not a guarantee provided here. Classifier files and
#6456's workflows are untouched.

Other reserved workflows remain owned by their current lanes: discord-modal-deploy,
supabase-staging, supabase-production, production-package-resume,
release-please-transient-retry and security-checks/classifier. No App migration is
planned for them under this narrow purpose. Setup-node and action-hardening changes
also remain with their owners.

## Inventory and verification

Generate a current audit report on demand:

```sh
node scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-inventory.js > tmp/tuturuuu-bot-inventory.md
```

The generator prints workflow/script decisions and explicit current scopes. Its
output is a local report, not a committed snapshot or a global equality CI gate.
Unrelated workflow/script changes therefore do not make this PR's tests drift.
Policy tests reject any workflow reference to `TUTURUUU_BOT_` or
`tuturuuu-bot-token`, including non-minting jobs and comments. Any future Actions
proposal must separately review this local-only guard and the required environment
boundary before enabling minting; no workflow is currently authorized to use it.

Run focused tests through the shared resource queue:

```sh
ttr resources run -- node --test --test-concurrency=2 scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-token.test.js scripts/ci/tuturuuu-bot-workflows.test.js scripts/ci/release-please-auto-approve.test.js
```

Independent security review and exact-head CI remain integration gates. Mocked
Keychain/API tests do not prove a live installation, owner ACLs, rulesets or a
future environment's deployment-branch policy.
